key_insight: Reinforcement learning can improve code speed, but only if correctness, timing reward design, and training stability are made robust enough to overcome noisy execution measurements.
engineering_relevance: The paper shows how to turn execution time into a usable optimization objective for program synthesis systems, which is directly relevant to compiler-like code generation, automated refactoring, and high-performance code assistants.
method: Build DMC-Optim with large optimization tests and a calibrated sandbox for more reliable timing.
Compose correctness and speed into the RL reward, then use an offline simulator to choose promising configurations.
Adapt GRPO and evaluation for sparse, noisy timed-execution rewards.
evidence_signal: On DMC-Optim, strict top-50% pass@1 rises from 18.0% to 31.3% on Qwen 2.5 7B and from 30.7% to 50.4% on CWM 32B, with stronger gains at stricter percentiles.
watch_item: Performance depends on timing-sandbox quality, so degraded measurement environments can destabilize training and reduce the reliability of speed-based rewards.
